title: The Seminar on a Broad Claim: Testing Limits and Fixing Personal Grammar Errors · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: Dr. Lin: Thank you all for coming to this seminar. Our goal today is not to defend a broad conclusion but to test its limits. The claim on the screen says: “Remote work always increases productivity.” I want us to treat that sentence as a hypothesis, not a fact. We will look for cases where it holds, cases where it fails, and cases where we simply do not have enough information. Please write down one example from your own workplace before we begin. Maya: I work for a small design studio. When we moved to remote work, our weekly output rose for about three months. Then two new clients joined, and our communication became messy. I would say remote work helped at first, but the effect did not last. It depends on how many people need to talk to each other. Dr. Lin: That is a useful boundary condition. Notice that Maya is not saying remote work is bad.
prompt:
Part 1
Do you often work in a team?
What makes communication easy for you?
Do you prefer short tasks or long tasks?
How do you check your own mistakes?

Part 2
Describe a time when a plan did not work as expected. You should say: what the plan was; who was involved; what changed; and what you learned from it.

Part 3
Why do people sometimes make a claim too broad?
How can a team test a new idea safely?
Is it better to change a plan early or late? Why?
How can we separate personal preference from performance?
